laat_vaar.rede_vinder: No animals have been mentioned yet in this block, so 'die diere' has no antecedent; 'hulle' ties the animals to the family just named.
laat_vaar.rede_keurder: 'Die diere' on a farm homestead reads naturally in Afrikaans without a prior mention, while 'hulle' after a singular 'die familie' and a plural 'hutte' adds a number mismatch and a possible second referent, so the proposal is not clearly better.

vlae.teks: Die eerste boere se hoofgewasse was sorghum en giers.
vlae.rede: The protected entry for 'in Suider-Afrika' quotes this very sentence as the one that must stay bounded, but in this block it stands without the bound (only the first block says 'in Suider-Afrika'); read alone it may sound like a worldwide claim. Adding the bound is a content decision, so it is flagged, not changed.

laat_vaar_vorige.voor: gebou van wat naby te kry was
laat_vaar_vorige.na: gebou met wat hulle naby kon kry
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_vinder: 'gebou van wat naby te kry was' reads wooden; 'met wat hulle naby kon kry' is the natural construction with the same meaning.
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_keurder: 'gebou van wat naby te kry was' is natural idiomatic Afrikaans; the proposal is a lateral move.

laat_vaar_vorige.voor: potskerwe, wat stukke van gebreekte kleipotte is
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_vinder: A plain apposition is smoother than the relative clause ending in 'is', and 'stukkies' matches the glossary definition of potskerf.
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_keurder: The relative clause is standard Afrikaans and states the definition plainly for a Grade 5 reader; the apposition is only different.

laat_vaar_vorige.voor: het op 'n opstal gewoon, wat ook 'n plaasopstal genoem word.
laat_vaar_vorige.na: het op 'n opstal gewoon. Dit word ook 'n plaasopstal genoem.
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_vinder: The relative clause stands after the verb, far from 'opstal', so 'wat' can be read as referring to the whole clause; a separate sentence makes the reference clear and is easier for Grade 5.
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_keurder: A relative clause placed after the verb is normal Afrikaans and here can only refer to 'opstal'; splitting it is a lateral move.

laat_vaar_vorige.voor: het saam 'n dorpie gevorm, wat ook 'n boeredorpie genoem word.
laat_vaar_vorige.na: het saam 'n dorpie gevorm. So 'n dorpie word ook 'n boeredorpie genoem.
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_vinder: Same loose 'wat' after the verb; a separate sentence ties the alternative name clearly to 'dorpie'.
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_keurder: Same standard extraposed relative clause, clearly tied to 'dorpie'; the split only reads differently and repeats 'dorpie'.

laat_vaar_vorige.rede_vinder: 'Vars grond' calques English 'fresh ground'; 'nuwe grond' is the natural Afrikaans for land not yet farmed, with the same meaning.
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_keurder: 'Vars grond' contrasts naturally with 'uitgeboer', and 'nuwe grond' would put 'nuwe' twice in one clause before 'n nuwe dorpie'.

laat_vaar_vorige.blok: Lewende hawe: beeste, skape en bokke
laat_vaar_vorige.voor: Die diere het vir die familie melk
laat_vaar_vorige.na: Die diere het vir die families melk
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_vinder: The block opens with 'die boere' (plural) and no single family has been introduced in it, so 'die familie' has no clear referent; the plural matches the subject.
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_keurder: The lesson is built around one family introduced in the first block, so 'die familie' has a clear referent and reads naturally; the plural is a lateral move that shifts the picture from one family to many.
